title: Topic Grid by School (H1 & H2)
doc: 1 Topic Grid by School (H1 & H2) v0.7.docx

sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: One table for H1 (Q1–Q6) and one for H2 (P1 Q1–Q6, P2 Q1–Q4). Rows are school + year, sorted by school then year.
Each cell gives the syllabus Key Question(s) the question tests, e.g. '1.1.1b SUD: Urban population trends'.
Labels were assigned from the reading notes (question wording + marks of every sub-part), not from the answer schemes.

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: The 2026 syllabuses (8834, 9173) are used for all three years, including the 2024 and 2025 papers.
Key Questions are coded a, b, c in the order they appear in the syllabus, under each sub-topic (e.g. 1.1.1a/b/c).
Structured questions: every sub-part is given a Key Question; the cell lists each one once, ordered by marks (highest first). Ties follow sub-part order.
Essays: normally one Key Question; two only when the question clearly spans two.

Fieldwork questions are labelled by the syllabus fieldwork area (H1: Community response to climate change, Needs of the elderly; H2 adds Fluvial flood risk). Scenarios outside these areas are filed as 'Others'.
VJC 2026 H1 is left out (question paper is password-protected). MI 2026, NJC 2024 and RVHS 2024–2026 have no H1 paper in the sources.
Where a school's paper and answer scheme disagree on marks, the question paper's marks were used.
Errors printed in the schools' own papers are not listed here (as you asked earlier); they are recorded in the reading notes if needed.

sections.title: 6. To review: other points
bullets: TMJC 2026 H2 P1 Q2(e) (where Amazon deforestation happens, 4 marks) matches no syllabus Key Question, so it carries no code in its cell.

Two questions really cross clusters, so their cells show codes from both: CJC 2025 H2 P1 Q2 (Nile/GERD – includes 1.1.3b transboundary water) and HCI 2025 H2 P1 Q1 (Medog dam – includes 2.2.3c delta ecosystem services).

Recurring boundary calls, applied the same way everywhere: 'interdependence/interconnectedness' parts → 1.2.2a; monsoon rainfall explained through the ITCZ → 2.1.1c; how sea-level rise happens → x.2.2a (effects of CC); ice-sheet changes as a driver → x.2.1b.

sections.title: 7. To consider
bullets: Add a summary table: how often each Key Question was tested, by year (useful for spotting 'due' topics).
Shade cells by cluster or topic so patterns stand out when printed.
Add a short focus line under each code (e.g. 'Nike', 'London Docklands') to help recall the question.
Split the H2 table into separate Paper 1 and Paper 2 tables to make it less dense.
